leads.name: video-scoring-audio
leads.benefit: Compose short cues that reach specific picture beats, then measure loudness and duration against a timeline.
leads.difference: Uses explicit note-onset timing and acoustic verification where text-to-music timecode prompts are unreliable.
leads.risk: Requires soundfont/MIDI/fluidsynth/ffmpeg helpers, downloads, audio output writes and possibly paid Lyria network calls. Root MIT does not license soundfonts.

leads.name: lilypond-score-editor
leads.benefit: Edit and engrave printed music, parts, lead sheets, tabs and MIDI from LilyPond notation.
leads.difference: Targets score preparation, error repair and part extraction rather than generating a song from a prompt.
leads.risk: Root license absent; writes user score files and uses Python, LilyPond, optionally PyYAML and Scheme. No authority for local edits or execution implied.

leads.name: music
leads.benefit: Create instrumental music and electronically generated arrangement plans from textual direction.
leads.difference: A specific production backend and composition-plan API, not proof of harmony, melody or EDM craftsmanship.
leads.risk: API key/account, paid calls, optional uploads, storing generated assets and fine-tuning. No automatic onboarding, billable requests or content uploads without consent.

leads.name: design-concept-art-brief
leads.benefit: Give artists a usable brief covering visual tone, silhouettes, variations, deliverables and rights.
leads.difference: Pre-production art-direction contract, not image generation or an illustration finished by the skill.
leads.risk: Cites books/studio methods and unverified 40-60% savings; cannot assert those statistics. Artist references and reference images retain their own rights.

leads.name: editorial-line-system
leads.benefit: Turn written ideas into restrained black-and-white line-art characters and magazine-style layouts.
leads.difference: Explicit editorial visual language with style consistency and text-rendering tradeoffs.
leads.risk: Root license absent (NOASSERTION); defaults to calling an image-generation tool and may produce external output. Need license, host and output rights before adaptation or installation.

leads.name: scenario-storyboards
leads.benefit: Create a comic or storyboard as separately reviewed panels with consistent characters and readable lettering.
leads.difference: Panel-by-panel script, locked cast, then assembly, rather than one uneditable page image.
leads.risk: Requires multiple Scenario sibling skills, account/model access, paid generation, image uploads and output writes. Needs consent for every external action.

leads.name: scenario-identity-library
leads.benefit: Keep character or prop identity stable across drawings by establishing approved reference views.
leads.difference: Named cast/reference library and turnaround consistency; covers character side only, not environment art.
leads.risk: Creates persistent named Scenario collections, uploads/generates images, and consumes paid model calls. Requires action-specific approval, particularly for personal reference photos.

known_rights_failures.risk: Generated outputs and uploaded source imagery have independent rights; persistent collections not authorized
